OTT · Dual-brand streaming · 2024

One app, two content worlds.

A global movie and drama streaming platform wanted to launch a second content library — Indian films and dramas — inside its existing app, without it feeling bolted on, and without splitting into two products.

EngagementFreelance · 6 months
PlatformMobile · iOS & Android
My roleUX · UI · Dev handoff
01Context

Two content libraries, one subscription.

The client runs Lionsgate Play, an international movies-and-dramas streaming app. They were launching Tiger TV — an Indian films-and-dramas vertical with its own separate subscription — and wanted it to live inside the same app rather than ship as a standalone product.

I came on as the sole designer for this, covering research, UX, UI, a small supporting design system, and handoff to the client's dev team.

02Users & role

Two audiences, one account.

World A · Existing catalogue

Existing subscribers

Came to the app for its original catalogue. Needed the core experience to stay familiar — the new content shouldn't crowd their home feed or feel like a different app took over.

World B · Indian content

New Indian-content audience

Drawn specifically to the Indian dramas and films. Needed to feel like this library had its own identity and curation — not a folder buried inside someone else's app.

UX researchUI researchInformation architectureUser flowsDesign system (new)Design tokensComponentsTypographyColor & themingSpacing / layoutPrototypingDev handoff
03Problem

Sell a second subscription without losing the first.

Lionsgate subscribers came for Hollywood — most had never heard of Tiger TV, and asking someone who already pays to pay again is exactly where people churn. Tiger TV was a separate Indian-content plan that had to earn that second yes.

“

The design problem: make Tiger TV discoverable and worth a second subscription — from inside the same app, with its own identity and curation — without diluting the Lionsgate experience or reading as a money grab. Two brands, two paywalls, one app.

04Approach

One shared shell, two theme layers.

One app shell — account, navigation and structure shared — with two theme layers on top. Each world gets its own accent, imagery and curation rhythm, while the underlying skeleton stays identical.
